newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament slams Israel over new settlements. [CORRECTED 18:46 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament slams Israel over new settlements. [CORRECTED 18:46 GMT]

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday added its voice to widespread criticism of Israel's decision to build a Jewish settlement of some 6,500 houses in Arab East Jerusalem.

"Such action is bound to have a negative impact on the peace negotiations (with the Palestinians)," the European Union assembly said in a resolution deploring the decision and demanding a halt to the project.

The resolution, supported by Euro-deputies from across the political divide, reminded the government of Israeli Prime Minister (corrects from "president") Benjamin Netanyahu that the Middle East peace accords committed Israel and the Palestinians to reach an agreement on the final status of Jerusalem.
Neither side should attempt to alter their position in East Jerusalem before those negotiations, due to begin next week, had been completed, the parliament insisted.
The Israeli decision would make the search for peace even more complicated and trigger new violence which would be very hard to quench, warned Spanish Socialist Carmen Diez de Rivera.
Dutch Liberal Jan Bertens slammed the decision as "foolish".
While it did not breach the letter of the Oslo peace accord, it certainly violated its spirit and would, he said, do the conservative government "more harm than good in the long term".

Israel views Jerusalem as its undivided capital while the Palestine Liberation Organisation regards East Jerusalem, captured by the Jewish state in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

The EU's commissioner for the Middle East, Manuel Marin, said that as far as the EU was concerned, "the settlements and the Occupied Territories go against international law and do comprise a very serious obstacle to the peace process".
"The Union cannot, nor should not, accept that East Jerusalem be considered part of the territory and sovereignty of Israel," Marin told the parliament.
